title.en: The genitive case: of, without, and nothing

card: The genitive means ***of***: **кни́га бра́та** (*brother's book*), **стака́н воды́** (*a glass of water*). It also follows **нет** (*there isn't*), most quantities, and many prepositions: **у, из, от, без, для, до, по́сле, о́коло**. Singular endings: **-а/-я** for masculine and neuter, **-ы/-и** for feminine.

sections.body: The genitive is the most frequent case after the nominative, because it does so many jobs: possession, parts and amounts, absence, and a long list of prepositions. Its common thread is *of* or *from*: something belongs to, comes out of, or is measured from the word in the genitive.

Genitive
Examples
rows: -ы (-и after к, г, х, ж, ш, щ, ч)

sections.title: The main uses
sections.body:
- **Possession and *of***: **маши́на отца́** (*father's car*), **центр го́рода** (*the city centre*), **ча́шка ча́я** (*a cup of tea*).
- **Absence with нет**: **У меня́ нет вре́мени.** **Здесь нет метро́.** In the past and future the verb becomes neuter and impersonal: **не́ было вре́мени**, **не бу́дет вре́мени**.
- **Quantities**: **мно́го**, **ма́ло**, **ско́лько**, **не́сколько**, and numbers from 2 up (see the numbers article): **мно́го рабо́ты**, **два бра́та**.
- **Prepositions**: **у** (*by, at someone's*), **из** (*out of*), **от** (*from a person, away from*), **без** (*without*), **для** (*for*), **до** (*until, up to*), **по́сле** (*after*), **о́коло** (*near*), **кро́ме** (*except*).
- **Having**: **у меня́ есть** (*I have*) literally means *by me there is*: **У бра́та есть маши́на.**

English *'s* and *of* map onto the genitive, but the word order flips: *Anna's brother* is **брат А́нны**, the owner coming **after**. English *any* in negatives also hides a genitive: *There aren't any problems* is **Нет пробле́м**.

The 7-letter rule again: after **к, г, х, ж, ш, щ, ч** the feminine ending is **-и**, not **-ы**: **кни́ги**, **ру́чки**, **да́чи**. Spelling errors here are among the most common in learners' writing.
**нет** wants the genitive because nothing is there: the thing is *missing*, so it can't be the subject. **Ма́ма до́ма** → **Ма́мы нет до́ма**. The subject vanishes into the genitive.

mistakes.why: **нет** takes the genitive; **вре́мя** has the special genitive **вре́мени**.
The owner is genitive. **па́па** declines like a feminine **-а** noun: **па́пы**.

examples.en: I'm drinking a cup of tea.
I take my coffee without sugar.
